title: De altitudine columnarum sub proprio pondere corruentium

deep.reconstruction:
Context: E510 asks for the greatest height a column can reach before it buckles under its own weight. Euler reduces the buckling condition to the vanishing of P(1+Q') − QP'. Here P, P', Q, Q' are four alternating power series in a parameter t, which lumps together height, weight and stiffness. The previous page (§32) gave log-recurrences for the terms of P and P'; this page (§33) gives them for Q and Q'. Section 34 then explains the trial-and-error search. By the 'previous dissertation' t < 266, so Euler starts at t = 200 and watches the sign of P(1+Q') − QP' to decide whether to raise or lower t (a regula-falsi / bisection root search).

Decoding the tabulated constants, which are base-10 logarithms:
- Q: I = t/6 (log 6 = 0.7781513).
- For n ≥ 2 the ratio of successive terms is |Q_n/Q_{n-1}| = t·(3n−2)(3n−1)(3n)/(3n−3). The constants are log 40, log 84, log 146.67, log 227.5, log 326.4, …, log 3602.1.
- Hence |Q_n| = t^n · 3·6·9···(3n−3)/(3n)!.
- The companion series has Q'_n = Q_n/(3n+1), i.e. the factors 1/4, 1/7, 1/10, …, 1/61.
- By the same decoding of §32, |P_n| = t^{n−1} · 1·4·7···(3n−5)/(3n−2)!, with ratio t(3n−4)(3n−3)(3n−2)/(3n−5). Also P'_n = P_n/(3n−1).
- The next page shows that the terms alternate in sign.

These are power series of the kind that come from a linear ODE with a coefficient linear in the arc variable (Airy/Bessel-of-order-1/3 type), evaluated at the column's end. The tables simply let each term be computed from the previous one by adding log t and subtracting a constant. The page is purely computational scaffolding.
errors: Row XIII of the Q-table: the printed constant 3,1727474 should be 3,1827474. Check: 38·39·37/36 = 1523.1667 and log10(1523.1667) = 3.1827474. Every other constant on the page checks to 7 decimals. It is a one-digit misprint (7 for 8). Whether it affects the later numerical evaluation depends on whether Euler used the wrong value; for t around 200 the term is already tiny, so the effect would be negligible.

ideas.what: Log-recurrence tables for the successive terms of the alternating power series Q and Q' = Σ Q_n/(3n+1), with |Q_n| = t^n·3·6···(3n−3)/(3n)!
ideas.modern_name: Power-series (Frobenius-type) solution of an Airy/Bessel-type ODE, evaluated term by term with logarithms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard 18th-century practice; the correct self-weight buckling solution through Bessel functions is credited to Greenhill (1881)
ideas.where_published: E510 itself (Acta Acad. Sci. Imp. Petrop. 1778, publ. 1780); the series method also appears in Euler's companion papers on columns

ideas.what: Determining the critical parameter t by trial values and the sign change of P(1+Q') − QP'
ideas.modern_name: Root bracketing / regula falsi for the characteristic (determinant) equation of an eigenvalue problem

deep.surprise_reason: The page holds only numerical auxiliary tables for series evaluation. The only finding is a one-digit misprint in one log constant. The history of Euler's self-weight column work, including its difficulties and Greenhill's later correct solution, is already discussed by Truesdell.
